text: Do you ever enter a room in Boulders's
Gate and feel bored? Probably not, since
nearly every building has a secret
passage, hidden combat encounter,
handsome politician, or murder basement
to help flesh out the story in the
world. Sometimes it feels like the devs
thought of everything, which made me
wonder, does this city have any truly
boring areas? Locations which don't
respect your time, offer little as far
as RPG rewards go, and most importantly,
lack purpose. As someone who
professionally answers questions no one
asked, I took to the streets to find
out. The lower city is the focus today,
and by my count, there are 43 unique
shops, homes, or structures within the
region to explore. But before we look
inside these places, I wanted to look
underneath them at the city's basement.
In many games, these neglected rooms are
hardly worth your time. But here,
they're full of murder. How much murder,
you ask? Well, by my count, 11 out of 34
of the city's basements contain either a
corpse, dismembered limb, or other
evidence that a murder took place
within. Meaning roughly 1/3 of Bulerian
basements can be classified as murder
basements, just slightly above the North
American average. Even if it is a little
bit overdone, murder isn't really
boring. To most people, discovering a
crime sparks curiosity. There's a reason
the news is often full of heinous crimes
and not pointless everyday annoyances.
Crime is just more interesting. And
should you also include the more serious
Baldderian basement crimes such as
forgery, smuggling, eating children, and
the lengthy list of the Shauns are
doing, that number increases to 18 out
of 34 basements, just over half of all
underground structures. As a side note,
I'm not a police officer, nor did I
study law, but I did watch CSI, so I
feel I'm just as qualified as any cop
I've ever met. Were we to also include
booby traps or other less serious but
still likely illicit activities to my
list, then roughly 33 out of 34
basements are actively breaking the law,
as the vast majority of homes have
secret basements leading to exploding
chests, absurd lethal gas traps, or
other bizarre dangerous contraptions.
Even the wholesome Hibberry family, who
take care of orphan children, have a
trap chest in their basement ready to
injure a would-be criminal or an
unsupervised curious child.
By my findings, only one basement in the
entire city has nothing obviously
strange, illegal, or questionable at all
going on. Just who is this heroic normie
in our city of crime? Well, it's none
other than Damon from the Diabolic
Forge. If you want to get technical, his
basement is shared with the Devil's Fee,
who does have a little bit of weird
stuff going on, but it's separated by a
wall, so I'll treat it as a unique
location. Damon's shop basement has no
traps, no quests, no combat, and most
importantly, no murder. Oddly enough,
his chests aren't even locked. And he's
such a nice guy that he won't even
consider it stealing should you pick up
the many plus two weapons littered about
his underground workshop. It's just a
standard blacksmith room and Damon
appears to be a pretty decent dude.
Nothing interesting whatsoever. Other
homes have hidden safe behind paintings,
secret walls, unique furniture, and of
course murder. But Damon has nothing.
And you know what? I'm okay with that.
Even if it is just likely that his forge
was cut content, he can have the award
for the most standard and slightly
boring basement in the city. While
inspecting the city's many basements, I
was pleasantly surprised to discover two
of which I'd never seen before. The
music shop with this interesting piano
mechanism which opens a door and
contains an absurd amount of lethal
traps that defend its musical
instruments. And the other being the
Gulbraith home, an underground mind
flare Hunter's Lair who has the only
usable katana in the game. Not a strong
weapon, but it is pretty neat. If you've
never explored the city's basements
before, I highly recommend taking a tour
as they all had a lot of love put into
them by the developers, unlike many
other video game basements. So, back to
the original question. Is Damon's
basement the most boring location in the
entire city? I think it's certainly a
contender. There must be a bigger waste
of time somewhere else. Let's expand our
search to places which at a glance are
pointless. The areas of the city which
appear to have no quests, no interesting
story, just nothing. But in a game like
BG3, this can be kind of tough because
if you visit a place like the Ambersted
home, you might find an average family
innocent of any crime without even a
murder basement and nothing noteworthy
to investigate. But had you chose to
help feed a mind flare a corpse back in
the Rivington windmill, ignored the
emperor's instructions to kill it, and
just carried on with your adventure, you
might visit here later to discover that
same mind flare came in and ate the
inhabitants. What most players who came
here saw as a normal questless pointless
home, became a dark example of player
agency. A similar tale can be said for
the Society of Brilliance, which can
either be a blood text wet dream or a
place for study, depending only on if
you gave an old racist Karen an egg 30
hours earlier in your playthrough.
There's also Lady Janet's mansion, which
becomes a relatively normal Gordon
Ramsay reference.
>> You served this to Lady Janith. It's
raw.
>> Or a nightmare fueled haunted house
where the furniture flies at your face.
It really just depends on what you
decided to do. Hell, even the bell
towers, which players assume did nothing
for over a year, have a hidden mechanic
attached to them where if you kill the
specific comedian in the tavern, go ring
the bell in each tower, then return to
your camp in Rivington, you will find an
egg behind the chicken coops, unlocking
an explosive sheep companion. And
there's honestly not even any
explanation as to why. Larry, what the
hell is this?
What I'm really saying here is that most
of the boring locations in this game are
only boring because you didn't discover
the dark, terrible secrets hidden behind
their walls. But if you really want to
get down to it, out of these 43ish entry
lower city buildings, there's only one
without anyone to talk to or buy things
from, without secrets, devoid of any
quests, and really lacking a purpose.
Old Joel's house. A single standalone
one room home locked and desolate. While
the studio abode may lack in all that,
even this empty home appears to at least
show some character. A note asking the
police to keep away.
>> This is Joel's house. No letters, no
clerics, no herb sellers, no potion
peddlers, and no steel watch.
>> In a city filled with interesting
things, it's the beacon of an average
uninteresting normal millennialsized
home. And yet, its owner, old Joel, is
nowhere to be seen. Just where is Joel?
What happened to Joel? Why does Joel
hate the police? all things we'll never
know. His home is likely the most boring
house in the entire game. And here I am
still left with questions I wish I knew
to answers about an NPC which doesn't
even exist. Joelstead is another
contender for the most boring place. But
our search isn't over yet. Next, we'll
take a look at the outdoors, a place I
would never go in real life. But in this
game, everywhere you look outside, there
are people to talk to. Kind of to the
point that it's overwhelming and pretty
much impossible to do the usual RPG
approach of talking to every single NPC
to learn obscure hints and find some
cool side quests. I bet a lot of people
don't even know that you can help find a
cat to adopt for Darth Bonecloak or take
on a quest to get Wilburn's head for
this city guard because talking to
everyone in act three is not viable. The
outdoor rooftops are mostly
uninteresting, but they do at least have
Tara the traveling tresome vendor to
make up for that a bit. And as players,
we don't really expect much from the
roofs anyways. So, I feel if you had to
pick just one outdoor area as a
contender for the boring list, it's
likely near the lower city beach with a
swagan ambush, a world-saving fish, and
this orc who discusses having stolen
nine sacks of flour that morning and
actually carrying said nine sacks of
flour. This beach has the type of world
building that I love to see. It's not at
all a boring place. However, if we look
over the water to this random corner of
the map that looks like you're not even
supposed to go here, you'll find a tiny
empty beach with a dead tree. And for
some reason, you can jump over here and
access the beach. This is the type of
boring I wanted to show off in this
video. An area the developers forgot
about with nothing at all. Except it
isn't. There are no survival roles or
other clues to lead you to this, but
digging here will reveal a chest with
some loot and a skeleton. Just who is
this? Perhaps old Joel?
No, no, no. There's no evidence of that.
We don't know who this is, and we'll
likely never know. But the fact that a
beach that looks inaccessible has what I
believe is the only dig location without
any survival checks at all is pretty
interesting. Amazing. Nah, probably not.
But is it boring? Not to me. And that's
really the point of this video. Tricking
you into thinking there's going to be
some super boring place that devs forgot
about, but actually showing you how
rewarding exploration in this game
really is. That this game respects your
time and there are cool little secrets
hidden everywhere. Even the areas you're
not supposed to be able to go to, like
the developer asylums, have some rather
eye-catching things. But after exploring
everywhere in the entire game, I feel
there is exactly one place where this
does not hold true. A location which is
such a letdown that players refuse to
believe that there's nothing there. And
many people spend countless hours
searching for a non-existent secret
hidden within. An area so obscure that
you expect a great reward only to be
slapped in the face. I'm talking, of
course, about Kazador's basement. No,
not the cool one with a boss fight, a
great conclusion to a companion story
line, and a secret story boy within a
coffin. I'm talking about his other
basement. To get there, you got to first
open the door with his ring. Slay the
werewolves. Get the key from the attic.
Return to the main floor. Push the
button in the tiny room with one
character. Then use a second character
to go back and visit the unlocked secret
room in the opposite corner. Underneath
the chest, there's a hidden hatch. Using
that key leads to a new basement with a
small puzzle to open the door, followed
by another puzzle with a second locked
door. Then a third and final room, which
has a bunch more traps leading to
another chest, which can't be moved or
picked up. By placing items on the
weight triggers, you can unlock the
chest. And unlocking the chest reveals
some basic loot with a confession
written by another NPC who doesn't
exist. Multiple puzzles, several hard to
find pathways, and it's all for a chest
with some basic loot and no additional
substance to the story. The funniest
part of this is that it's so out of the
ordinary for Balders's Gate to have a
room like this that's just completely
pointless. There are now dozens of
threads online on Reddit, forums, and
YouTube videos all discussing it. How
could there possibly be nothing here?
This was made worse by the fact that
Larry wrote in a previous patch note
that they fixed the puzzle to make it
now solvable, which is technically true,
but all they did was remove a bunch of
old broken levers from the room that had
no function and further confused players
who came here as many people have came
here and wasted time trying to solve a
secret puzzle which doesn't even seem to
exist. In conclusion, yes, there is a
boring location in Balders's Gate. And
this is it. the one and only area which
doesn't respect your time, has no
redeeming qualities, no combat
encounters, no one to talk to, no
quests, doesn't help flesh out the world
in any way, and is apparently so secret
that the developers themselves forgot to
put something interesting inside.
Casador already has an interesting
basement that explains everything the
place had going on. This entire location
is pointless. Compared to the other
boring contenders, you can forgive the
rooftops for being empty. Most are in
real life. Damon's workshop being
ordinary, understandable. He's a normal
dude. Old Joel's home being vacant isn't
really a concern. But Kazador's mansion,
with its intricate puzzles, hard to spot
entrance, and entirely new loaded area
having nothing just doesn't hold up when
compared to the rest of the game. And
it's for that reason I believe it's the
only area worthy of being called boring
in Bulg's Gate. Honestly, a pretty
impressive feat when you look at how
much content there really is. And
realistically, compared to other games,
hardly a major flaw. But I'd be curious
about what you guys think. Am I a
complete idiot? Is there another
location I missed? Let me know in the
comments below and I'll read it. Sorry
for the lengthy times between videos and
big thanks to my channel members for
still supporting me. Appreciate you
guys. Until next time, proxy out.
